newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway seeks to end fisheries row with Iceland.
newsitem.headline: Norway seeks to end fisheries row with Iceland.

text.p: Norway proposed to Iceland on Wednesday to strengthen fisheries cooperation to avoid a repetition of an incident involving an Icelandic fishing boat that clouded bilateral relations.

Norway's ambassador to Reykjavik, Nils Dietz, submitted an explanation to the Icelandic Foreign Ministry of the detention of the fishing boat Sigurdur by Norwegian coastguards in the North Atlantic, Foreign Ministry spokesman Ingvard Havnen said.
Icelandic Prime Minister David Oddsson had protested strongly to Norway on Tuesday about the incident, which occurred last Friday in a Norwegian fishing zone off Jan Mayen island.

"The main point in our reply is that Norway proposes to start discussions with Iceland with a view to strengthening cooperation in fisheries control to avoid this kind of incident happening again," Havnen told Reuters.

He said Norway wanted to improve monitoring of fisheries resources, boost the exchange of information, have reciprocal visits to the respective coastguards and ensure both countries had a common understanding of the regulations.
"If the discussions call for adjustments of the regulations we are open to considering that," Havnen said.
The Sigurdur was detained on suspicion of catching 400 tonnes of herring illegally, and was towed to the northern Norwegian town of Bodoe.

The captain, Kristbjoern Arnason, was fined 30,000 Norwegian crowns ($4,200) for violating Norwegian economic zone regulations and rules for fishing herring. The boat's owner, fishing company Isfelag, was fined 375,000 crowns on the same grounds.
The Icelanders refused to pay and the matter will come up in a Bodoe court on September 2.
While Iceland sent a diplomatic protest to Oslo over the detention, Norway sought to play down the incident, saying it was purely a matter of upholding regulations.

"We gave the Icelanders a factual description of the incident based on the reports from the coastguards and the police," Havnen said. "This is a matter for our judicial system. It would be unthinkable for Norwegian politicians to try to influence the legal proceedings."
Norway and Iceland have had several bitter disputes over fishing quotas and rights in the Barents Sea and the North Atlantic over the past few years.
The latest dispute centres on whether or not the Sigurdur, which has a license to fish off Jan Mayen, told Norwegian fisheries authorities about its intention to fish there.
The Norwegian coast guard service says the boat made no such announcement, but Iceland says it has verified that the ship radioed Norwegian authorities in line with regulations.
